source_text: Si haec ita se habent, ut veritas nobis adiudicetur, quicunque in ea regula incedimus, quam ecclesia ab apostolis, apostoli a Christo, Christus a deo tradidit, constat ratio propositi nostri, definientis non esse admittendos haereticos ad ineundam de scripturis provocationem, quos sine scripturis probamus ad scripturas non pertinere. Si enim haeretici sunt, Christiani esse non possunt, non a Christo habendo quod de sua electione sectati haereticorum nomina admittunt. Ita non Christiani nullum ius capiunt Christianarum litterarum, ad quos merito dicendum est: Qui estis? quando, et unde venistis? quid in meo agitis, non mei? quo denique, Marcion, iure silvam meam caedis? qua licentia, Valentine, fontes meos transvertis? qua potestate, Apelles, limites meos commoves? Mea est possessio. Quid hic, ceteri, ad voluntatem vestram seminatis et pascitis? Mea est possessio, olim possideo, prior possideo, habeo origines firmas ab ipsis auctoribus quorum fuit res. Ego sum haeres apostolorum. Sicut caverunt testamento suo, sicut fidei commiserunt, sicut adiuraverunt, ita teneo. Vos certe exhaeredaverunt semper et abdicaverunt ut extraneos, ut inimicos. Unde autem extranei et inimici apostolis haeretici, nisi ex diversitate doctrinae, quam unusquisque de suo arbitrio adversus apostolos aut protulit aut recepit?
thought_title: The Church's inheritance and the heretics' exclusion
orientation: Tertullian is speaking in his own voice, directly addressing heretics, claiming the apostolic inheritance of the Scriptures and denying heretics any right to them.
pass_a_gloss: If these things so hold themselves, that truth is adjudged to us, whoever walk in that rule which the church handed down from the apostles, the apostles from Christ, Christ from God, the reasoning of our proposition stands, defining that heretics are not to be admitted to entering a challenge from the Scriptures, whom without the Scriptures we prove not to pertain to the Scriptures. For if they are heretics, they cannot be Christians, not having from Christ that which, having followed from their own choice, they admit the names of heretics. Thus, not Christians, they take no right of Christian writings, to whom deservedly it must be said: Who are you? when, and from where did you come? what are you doing in my property, you who are not mine? by what right, finally, Marcion, do you cut down my forest? by what license, Valentinus, do you divert my springs? by what power, Apelles, do you move my boundaries? Mine is the possession. Why do you, the rest, sow and feed here according to your will? Mine is the possession; I possess it long ago, I possess it first, I have firm origins from the very authors whose the matter was. I am the heir of the apostles. As they provided in their testament, as they entrusted to faith, as they bound by oath, so I hold. They certainly disinherited you always and renounced you as outsiders, as enemies. But from where are heretics outsiders and enemies to the apostles, except from the diversity of doctrine, which each one from his own judgment either brought forward or received against the apostles?

choices.why: Legal term for bringing a case; preserves the forensic force of the argument that heretics have no standing to dispute from Scripture.
The possessive 'meo' is substantival, referring to the church's inherited domain; 'property' makes the legal-ownership metaphor explicit.
Keeps the concrete image of unlawful use of another's land, matching the legal metaphor of possession and boundaries.
Preserves the water-source image and the sense of redirecting what belongs to another.
Boundary-stone language from Roman property law; 'move' keeps the literal force of 'commoves'.
Legal term for inheritance; the church claims the apostolic estate as its rightful heir.

pass_b_english: If this is how things stand, so that truth is adjudged to us who walk in that rule of faith which the church handed down from the apostles, the apostles from Christ, and Christ from God, then the reasoning of our position is established: we define that heretics must not be admitted to bring a challenge from the Scriptures, since we prove without the Scriptures that they have no claim to the Scriptures. For if they are heretics, they cannot be Christians, since they do not hold from Christ what they have followed by their own choice, and so they take on the name of heretics. Being therefore not Christians, they acquire no right to Christian writings, and to them it is rightly said: Who are you? When did you come, and from where? What are you doing on my property, you who are not mine? By what right, Marcion, do you cut down my forest? By what license, Valentinus, do you divert my springs? By what authority, Apelles, do you move my boundaries? The property is mine. Why do the rest of you sow and pasture here according to your own pleasure? The property is mine. I have possessed it from the beginning; I possessed it first. I hold firm origins from the very authors to whom the matter belonged. I am the heir of the apostles. As they provided in their testament, as they entrusted it to faith, as they bound it by oath, so I hold it. They certainly disinherited you always and renounced you as outsiders, as enemies. And why are heretics outsiders and enemies to the apostles, except because of the difference of doctrine, which each one by his own judgment either brought forward or received against the apostles?
